findings.message: `gate_owner` returns 12 when `consent_by_assignee` cannot read the tag history (`return 2`, so `|| return 12`). `status_row` puts 12 in the same bucket as 11 and maps both to `consent=other`. The row then reads as a definite "not-opted-in (fleet:auto not added by the assignee)" and counts as terminal, so `--watch` stops. `optin_decide` (`lib/optin.sh:10`) has the same root cause: it maps 12 to `readd`, so a failed history read makes optin untag the item's `fleet:auto`. Fix: split 12 out in both places. In status, set `consent=unknown`, show the record as `?` and never mark it terminal. In optin, return an error ("could not read the work item history").
findings.scenario: 002-a is assigned to alice, and alice added fleet:auto herself. The `updates` (history) call fails once (AzDO 500 or timeout). `status 002-a --watch` prints `not-opted-in (fleet:auto not added by the assignee)` with terminal=true and returns 0 while the run is still dispatching. In the same case, `optin 002-a` untags fleet:auto and re-tags it instead of stopping with an error.

findings.message: The fix that stops long paths reading as secrets only exempts values that start with `/`, `~/`, `./` or `../`. A relative path with no leading `./` still goes to the 52-character check, and `[A-Za-z0-9+/_-]` matches `/` and `-` across segments. `pipeline_file` is documented as a repo-relative path like `azure-pipelines/specclaw-fleet.yml`. Because `load_fleet_settings` runs at the top of `bin/specclaw-fleet`, the `die` takes down every subcommand, including doctor. Fix: apply the per-segment check to any slash-separated, path-like value, not only rooted ones.
findings.scenario: `fleet:\n  pipeline_file: azure-pipelines/specclaw-fleet-dispatch-hosted-production.yml`. The 58-character run before the `.` matches, so `specclaw-fleet doctor`, `status`, `optin` and `trigger` all die with "fleet.pipeline_file ... looks like a secret". The same happens for `kubeconfig: clusters/bistec-dev-uat/kubeconfig-for-isolated-tenant`.

findings.message: `pipeline_var` captures `[^\"#[:space:]]+`, so a quoted connection name with spaces is cut at the first space. Doctor then asks AzDO for the wrong name and reports a real, ready connection as missing. AzDO service connection names may contain spaces. Fix: when the value is quoted, capture everything up to the closing quote, and strip only a trailing ` #comment` from an unquoted value.
findings.scenario: The pipeline YAML has `  fleetKubeConnection: "Fleet K3s"` and the connection `Fleet K3s` exists and is ready. `specclaw-fleet doctor` queries `endpointNames=Fleet,...` and prints `missing service-connections: Fleet`, exit 1.

findings.message: The `optin` mode in PY_TAGS still treats any existing tag as consent. If the item is assigned to `<upn>` and already has the tag, it exits 10 and the CLI prints "Opted in ...". If the item is unassigned and tagged, it assigns but keeps someone else's tag. The fleet layer works around this with untag-then-optin, but the documented `specclaw-azdo-issue optin` subcommand reports success while consent stays invalid for the trigger/dispatch gate (`gate_owner`). Two copies of the consent rule disagree (B4). Fix: make the CLI enforce the same rule, or have it report that it did not add the tag itself and not print "Opted in".
findings.scenario: Item #42 is assigned to alice, and bob added fleet:auto. `specclaw-azdo-issue optin sc 049-x fleet:auto alice@contoso.com` exits 0 and prints "Opted in Work Item #42: assigned to alice@contoso.com, fleet:auto". A following `specclaw-fleet trigger 049-x` exits 4 with "fleet:auto was not added by the assignee".

findings.message: The dry-run message breaks when the item is already assigned. `${O_WHO:-assign to $2 and }` expands to the assignee's UPN, so the output reads "would keep the assignment and alice@contoso.comre-add fleet:auto ...". The test only checks a substring, so it passes. Fix: use `${O_WHO:+keep the assignment and }` alone, and add the `assign to $2 and ` text only when `O_WHO` is empty.

Ready connection names are compared to the configured names case-sensitively, but AzDO names are case-insensitive. A case difference between the pipeline YAML and AzDO is reported as missing. Lowercase both sides before taking the set difference.

The settings list does not mention the new `FLEET_CLUSTER_NAME`, `FLEET_PIPELINE_FILE` or `kubeconfig` (which maps to `KUBECONFIG`). It also does not say that `kube_context`/`kubeconfig` from config are ignored when `TF_BUILD` is set, which the README documents.
